The HEAT toolkit addresses stakeholder engagement by guiding users through the process of consulting and including diverse stakeholders in the design process. It emphasizes the importance of engaging different stakeholders, particularly marginalized and vulnerable groups, to understand the intended and unintended consequences of AI systems. The toolkit provides instructions on identifying relevant stakeholders and encourages meaningful and power-sensitive engagement, avoiding tokenism and participation-washing.

In terms of environmental sustainability, HEAT includes a dedicated section for assessing and mitigating the environmental impact of AI systems. It introduces methods for calculating the carbon footprint of AI models and conducting Life Cycle Analysis. The toolkit encourages users to rethink their product design with environmental considerations in mind, promoting more-than-human-centred design practices that acknowledge the interconnectedness of all living things and align human goals with non-human needs and environmental constraints.
